name: Kentucky
summary_text: Trans visitors to Kentucky stand under the United States federal framework on travel documents and screening. Executive Order 14168, signed 20 January 2025, defines sex for federal purposes as a male-female binary and bars self-selection of gender on passports and visas; the State Department has stopped processing the X marker, and new passports are issued only as M or F according to supporting documents. Visa discretion, including the February 2025 refusal pathway for trans athletes seeking entry for women's sporting events, and checkpoint screening procedures apply on arrival in Louisville, Lexington and elsewhere in Kentucky as they do in every other state.  Kentucky's own instrument is Senate Bill 150, enacted on 29 March 2023 when the Kentucky General Assembly voted to override Governor Andy Beshear's veto. The statute does two things relevant here: it restricts which bathrooms transgender students may use in public schools, and it bans gender-affirming medical care for transgender minors in the commonwealth. It is the single 2023 statute carrying the school facility restriction.  Implementation runs through local school districts. In April 2023 the Kentucky Department of Education issued guidance to districts on applying the 2023 rules, advising them to remove sex education from the fifth-grade curriculum and to tread cautiously with the bathroom provisions. The department does not enforce the restriction directly; districts do.  The care prohibition took effect on 14 July 2023, when United States District Judge David Hale lifted the injunction he had issued the previous month. The order allows Kentucky to bar transgender minors from puberty blockers and hormone therapy. Seven transgender children and their parents had sued to block the statute, and the ACLU of Kentucky called the ruling a temporary setback.  The Movement Advancement Project's equality map catalogues Kentucky's 2023 K-12 facility ban among its state-by-state entries on bans against transgender people using public bathrooms and facilities according to their gender identity, placing the commonwealth within a national pattern rather than an isolated rule.

sources.title: Bourke v. Beshear (2013) and Love v. Beshear (2014)
sources.documents: Federal challenges to Kentucky's denial of marriage licenses to same-sex couples and refusal to recognize out-of-state same-sex marriages.
sources.detail: Bourke plaintiffs won recognition Feb 12, 2014; Love filed Feb 14, 2014, ruled July 2014 in U.S. District Court in Louisville; Sixth Circuit oral arguments Aug 6, 2014; External links lists 'Bourke v. Beshear, February 12, 2014'

sources.title: Kentucky Religious Freedom Act of 2013
sources.documents: Creates religious-exemption machinery allowing override of protections; requires state show 'clear and convincing evidence' to infringe 'sincerely held religious beliefs'; risk to local Fairness Ordinances.
sources.detail: Passed March 2013 both houses; supported by Kentucky Family Foundation and Kentucky Catholic Conference; opposed by Kentucky League of Cities, Kentucky Association of Counties, Kentucky ACLU, mayors of Louisville and Covington; Beshear veto overridden 79-15 House and 32-6 Senate

sources.title: EEOC v. R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes - U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
sources.documents: Core transgender-employment protection applicable in Kentucky; Title VII prohibits employment discrimination against transgender people; employers may not use RFRA to justify anti-LGBTQ discrimination.
sources.detail: Ruled March 7, 2018; Sixth Circuit covering Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio and Tennessee; facts: Aimee Stephens fired 2013 after disclosing transgender status/transition; boss said 'gender transition violat[es] God's commands'

sources.title: Kentucky hate-crime statutes and Kingdom Come State Park beating prosecution
sources.documents: Enforcement gap: statutes cover hate crimes based on sexual orientation but not gender identity; documents violent anti-gay attack and federal intervention due to lack of local confidence.
sources.detail: March 15, 2012 Kentucky State Police assisted FBI arresting David Jenkins, Anthony Jenkins, Mable Jenkins, and Alexis Jenkins of Partridge for beating of Kevin Pennington April 2011 at Kingdom Come State Park near Cumberland; advocacy by Kentucky Equality Federation president Jordan Palmer lobbying U.S. Attorney for Eastern District of Kentucky Aug 2011

sources.title: House Bill 470 - 2023 ban on gender-affirming care for minors
sources.documents: Criminalizes/prohibits gender-affirming care for minors with no phaseout; enforcement status and protest crackdown relevant to trans visitor safety.
sources.detail: Introduced Feb 2023; House judiciary advanced March 2, 2023, full House passed same day; legislature passed version March 17, 2023; Gov. vetoed; GOP-led legislature overrode March 29 with simple majority; 19 protesters arrested for criminal trespassing; effective July 14, 2023; Sept 28, 2023 federal appeals judges allowed ban to remain pending challenge; Mason-Dixon poll 71% opposed, 21% favor cited
